title: Lyonnaise Potatoes (Sautéed Potatoes and Caramelised Onions)
summary: Fried potato slices are tossed through deeply caramelised onions for a rich, bistro-style side from Lyon. The slow-cooked onions give the dish most of its flavour, so it's worth taking your time with them.

ingredients.item: waxy or all-purpose potatoes (such as Yukon Gold), peeled and cut into 6 mm rounds
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Par-cook the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potato rounds with cold water, add the salt and vinegar, bring to the boil and simmer for about 4 minutes until just barely tender. The vinegar firms the pectin in the potato slightly, which keeps the rounds whole rather than falling apart when they're fried.

steps.title: Drain and dry
steps.text: Drain well and spread the rounds out on a towel to dry thoroughly. Any surface moisture left on the potato will stop it browning properly in the pan.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee in the pan over medium heat and cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and deep golden. Add a splash of water to lift the browned bits from the base of the pan, then tip the onions into a bowl.

steps.title: Fry the potatoes
steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of ghee in the same pan over medium-high heat and fry half the potato rounds in a single layer for 4-5 minutes per side until golden; repeat with the remaining ghee and potatoes. Ghee can take this higher heat without burning the way whole butter would, so the potatoes get properly crisp.

steps.title: Combine and serve
steps.text: Return all the potatoes and onions to the pan, toss together for 1-2 minutes to heat through, then season with the pepper, scatter over the parsley and serve.

tips: Simmer the potato rounds only briefly before frying — overcooking them at this stage makes them fall apart once they hit the hot pan.
Take your time with the onions; rushing the caramelising is the most common reason lyonnaise potatoes taste flat instead of richly sweet.
Dry the potato slices well before frying so they brown instead of steaming in the pan.
Fry the potatoes in batches rather than overcrowding the pan, or they'll turn soft instead of crisp.
storage: Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot frying pan over medium heat until piping hot and recrisped, as a microwave will leave them soft. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
